extra.message: case_bundle_thaw_187 deserializes attacker-controlled data with pickle.loads(raw), where raw comes from request.body (optionally base64-decoded). pickle.loads can execute arbitrary code during unpickling, leading to remote code execution.

extra.message: case_formula_cast_269 evaluates attacker-supplied input with eval(expr, ...) where expr comes directly from request.GET['expr']. extra.message: case_spool_fan_315 converts request.GET['count'] to an int and builds a materialized list of that many dicts ([... for idx in range(count)]). There is no upper bound, so a huge count (e.g. 10**9) causes memory exhaustion and denial of service.

extra.message: case_trust_drift_728 disables TLS certificate verification by using ssl._create_unverified_context() when calling urllib.request.urlopen. This makes the outbound HTTPS request vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks.

extra.message: case_xml_fold_736 parses attacker-supplied request.body XML with an lxml parser configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True and no_network=False. extra.message: case_trace_panel_745 returns internal configuration details in the JSON response, including os.environ.get('DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE') and str(BASE_EXPORT_DIR). This discloses the Django settings module and absolute server filesystem paths to callers.

extra.message: api_matter_detail fetches a Matter by pk and returns its full details without verifying the caller has access to that matter. Unlike api_matters (which scopes the list to lead_attorney/paralegals), any logged-in attorney or paralegal can read any matter by guessing/enumerating its pk (IDOR / broken access control), exposing other attorneys' sensitive matter data.
